facts.status_note: abandoned but still there, per firelookout.com; the Register gives no current condition

staffing.status: abandoned per firelookout.com; no staffing dates in sources read

events.note: NHLR and firelookout.com give 1934 (firelookout.com with a question mark); NHLR description says built sometime in the early 1930s; a May 31, 1934 newspaper item describes it as planned under a CCC project
registered April 13, 2022 as US 1554, MT 111; nominated by Kyle Stetler

corrections.why: The NHLR, firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts pages name the owner (Fort Belknap Tribe) but say nothing about visitor access or permission.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives 5,239 ft (1,597 m) and firelookout.com gives 5280 ft. The story reports both; the record's 1596.8 m matches the Register.

Register build field and firelookout.com give 1934 (the latter with a question mark); the Register description says early 1930s; the 1934 newspaper item describes a planned lookout. The record keeps 1934 and the story notes the uncertainty.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: three sources, one of them a single newspaper item quoted by Forest Lookouts (Choteau Acantha, May 31, 1934) that describes a plan, not a finished build. NHLR's description says little is known; firelookout.com gives only a short entry. Elevation conflict (5,239 vs 5,280 ft) noted. The record's access 'permission' has no source here; correction proposed to remove. record kind 'ground' not confirmed by any source read (sources say cupola-based / wooden cupola cabin), so it is left out of facts. Do not merge with us-mt-monument-peak.json: that file is the Helena-Lewis and Clark National Forest Monument Peak Lookout (CCC 1936, rented via recreation.gov), a different tower. The brief's coordinates (47.99295, -108.59646) match the NHLR; the west_us_lookouts coordinates in the conflict note were not checked. Not verified: current condition since firelookout.com's entry; whether any Fort Belknap access rules exist. No photos added (firelookout.com credits Luke Channer but gives no image URLs).
